title: Shiu et al. 2024 taste and antennal-grooming experiments, re-run on FlyWire v783
preregistration: Criteria, rates, trial counts and seeds were written before any run of this file. Dev seeds may be run while the code changes; held-out seeds are run once, on the commit that is reported, and their result is reported whatever it is. Thresholds marked 'ours' are not from the paper: the paper's own threshold for an activated neuron is a mean rate above 0 Hz over 30 trials.

protocol.notes: Shiu et al.'s defaults: 30 trials of 1000 ms, Poisson input at the stated rate to every neuron of the stimulated population. Their published populations were defined on materialization 630; ids absent from 783 are dropped and listed in the result.

criteria.claim: Sugar GRNs at 100 Hz activate MN9 in every simulation
criteria.quote: modelling using the correct connectome results in robust activation of MN9 in 100% of simulations when sugar-sensing neurons are activated at 100 Hz
criteria.threshold_note: active = MN9 fires at least once in the trial (ours); min 0.95 allows one quiet trial in 30 (ours)

criteria.claim: More neurons respond to stronger sugar GRN activation
criteria.quote: 45 are predicted to respond to 10 Hz sugar GRN activation, and 455 to 200 Hz (v630)
criteria.threshold_note: responders = neurons outside the stimulated set with mean rate > 0 Hz (the paper's definition); factor 3 (ours; the paper's ratio is 10)

criteria.claim: Shuffling the connectome's weights abolishes sugar-evoked MN9 activation
Bitter GRN activity inhibits sugar-evoked MN9 firing
criteria.quote: the addition of bitter GRN activity to sugar GRN activation in our model resulted in an inhibition of MN6 and MN9

criteria.claim: Ir94e GRN activity inhibits sugar-evoked MN9 firing
criteria.quote: Ir94e GRN activity inhibits proboscis extension
at a stimulation frequency at which each pathway activates MN9 at 40 Hz
criteria.threshold_note: the paper reaches 40 Hz MN9 at some water rate; 200 Hz is the highest it tested

criteria.claim: JO-CE neurons drive aBN1 robustly and JO-F neurons do not, despite synapsing onto it
criteria.quote: whereas JO-CE neurons will elicit robust aBN1 activity, JO-F neurons will not, despite synapsing directly onto aBN1
criteria.threshold_note: JO-F's mean aBN1 rate at most a quarter of JO-CE's (ours)

criteria.claim: Silencing the inhibitory neurons between JO-F and aBN1 lets JO-F drive aBN1
criteria.quote: JO-F activation with co-silencing of three inhibitory neurons
criteria.threshold_note: only 2 of the 3 published inhibitory ids exist in v783

criteria.claim: JON activation activates the antennal grooming neurons aBN1, aDN1 and aDN2
criteria.quote: the model identified that aBN1, aBN2, aDN1 and aDN2 respond to JON activation
criteria.threshold_note: respond = mean rate > 0 Hz over 30 trials (the paper's definition); aBN2 is not tested (no published ids)

criteria.claim: Degree-preserving rewiring abolishes sugar-evoked MN9 activation
criteria.threshold_note: control of ours, not in the paper

criteria.claim: A random graph of the same size and weights does not produce sugar-evoked MN9 activation
criteria.threshold_note: control of ours, not in the paper

criteria.claim: Permuting neuron signs disrupts sugar-evoked MN9 activation
criteria.threshold_note: control of ours, not in the paper
